sections.title: ## The retained local ramification calculation
sections.claim_text:
The detailed derivative and subgroup calculation is already independently checked in the A012 section of the 2026-11-05 galois-height REPORT and in the independent A012-SECOND-REVIEW. Those reports identify the inspected source as Serre, Local Class Field Theory, Chapter VI in Cassels--Frohlich, sections4.1--4.3, printed155--159, not the uninspected Local Fields book. Their substantive calculation is retained here.

For an extension of Q_p of degree at most a, its normal closure has degree at most a!. Over the maximal unramified subfield of that closure, an Eisenstein polynomial f of degree e for a uniformizer has derivative terms with distinct valuations modulo e. Consequently there is no cancellation at the minimum and v(f'(pi))<=e-1+e v_p(e). The derivative product over inertia conjugates and the lower-group definition give d_diff=sum_(i>=0)(|G_i|-1). Changing variables with the Herbrand function gives

    d_diff/e = 1-1/e + integral_(u>0)(1-1/|G^u|) du.

Before the last positive upper break the integrand is at least one half. The last break is therefore at most 2(1+log_2(a!))<=4a^2. The unramified and tame cases satisfy the same bound. For a Galois subfield F/Q_p, the exact subgroup rule is G_Qp^u intersect G_F = G_F^(psi_F/Qp(u)), with psi(u)>=u for u>=0. The inverse Herbrand function, not phi, is used. The two cited independent reports give the derivative proof of this indexing identity and the normal-closure justification.

At any p put F=L_v. Adjoin A[3], except at p=3 adjoin A[5]. The degree over Q_p is at most D G0: G0=|GL4(F5)| dominates |GL4(F3)|. Silverberg--Zarhin1995 Theorem3.5, printed406, has n>=3 and n prime to p; over F(A[n]) its required unramified torsion premise is satisfied by the identity extension. The A013 acceptance checks this exact scan and the semistability hypothesis. Pass to a normal closure if necessary. For ell different from p, semistability makes inertia unipotent. A stable ell-adic lattice shows that the pro-p wild image is finite, since the congruence kernel is pro-ell; a finite unipotent subgroup in characteristic zero is trivial. Thus absolute upper groups with u>U0 act trivially on V_ell(A) and lie in G_L.

On those groups the a_sigma mu_sigma factor is one. For odd p, chi is tame; beta squared is chi, so beta on wild pro-p inertia has order dividing two and is trivial. At p=2 the non-2 Dirichlet factors of chi are unramified and its possible factor modulo4 has order at most two on Q_2-units. Local reciprocity's norm compatibility gives chi|G_F(x)=chi(N_F/Q2(x)); apply it to the finite cyclic character field cut out by local chi. The retained norm-functoriality locator is Milne, Class Field Theory, v4.03, V Proposition3.3, printed157. Norms of units are units. Hence beta^4=chi^2=1 on O_F^*. This uses the finite-abelian norm functoriality itself, not only a quadratic example of it.

Write e=v_F(2)<=D. Logarithm and exponential are inverse on U_F^(e+1) and the ideal m_F^(e+1); the nonlinear series terms have strictly larger valuation there. Multiplication by four gives

    (U_F^(e+1))^4 = U_F^(3e+1).

Thus beta is trivial on U_F^(3e+1), its relative last upper break is at most 3e, and the subgroup rule makes it trivial on absolute upper groups above max(4D^2,3e)<=U0. This is the actual beta character over F, not a bound obtained from [L-prime:Q].

The two-dimensional r_ell therefore has tame invariant codimension at most two and Swan conductor at most 2U0. Possible infinite tame unipotent monodromy does not alter this wild integral. For every p and ell different from p,

    a_p(r_ell) <= 2+2U0 <= E0.

At a fixed point its tangent character is faithful, so the stabilizer is cyclic; its fixed point has a unique Hensel lift. These facts exclude new branch orbits or collisions. Pull back by J(u)=-57600F(u)^2/G(u)^6. The identity G^6-97200F^2=H^2 gives pullback multiplicities2,6,2; tame normalization leaves indices2,1,1. The discriminants and resultants have prime support at most13. The normalized cover therefore has degree at most324, is branched only at the six contacts, and locally has u-c=z^2 after unramified extension. Positive even contact valuation gives unramified specialization; negative valuation specializes at the unbranched infinity point. These are exactly the places encoded by M_S(u).

Since u is not a contact, its fiber is finite etale of degree at most324. Its splitting field K is normal over Q of degree at most324!, and the local calculation makes K unramified outside T=S union supp(M_S(u)). Choose a point of this fiber and pull back the universal abelian scheme to obtain the actual principally polarized O-surface A/K. sections.title: ## Precise algebraic statement
sections.claim_text:
Let A be an abelian surface over an algebraic closure of a characteristic-zero field. Suppose quasi-isogenies mu_sigma: sigma A -> A satisfy

    mu_sigma o sigma(mu_tau) = c(sigma,tau) mu_sigma_tau,

where c(sigma,tau) belongs to Q*. The rationality of this discrepancy is an input. It does not follow from the dimension of A alone. In particular it must be checked against the actual endomorphism algebra and chosen equivariance condition.

Use the usual degree of a genuine isogeny. The external input is Milne, Abelian Varieties, Arithmetic Geometry, Springer, 1986, Theorem 8.2 and its preceding paragraph, printed p. 115, with proof on p. 116: deg([n]_A)=n^(2 dim A), hence n^4 here, and multiplicativity of degree. The degree is the rank of a finite locally free map, which is unchanged under field conjugation. For negative n use the degree-one automorphism [-1]. The actual published pages were visually checked; their exact image hashes are in SOURCE-ATTACHMENT.md.

For a quasi-isogeny u define D(u)=deg([m]u)/m^4, where m is any positive integer clearing its denominators. This is independent of m. Indeed, if m and n both clear the denominators, then

    deg([n]([m]u)) = n^4 deg([m]u)
    deg([m]([n]u)) = m^4 deg([n]u),

and the two maps coincide. Thus their degrees coincide and the two quotients agree. A common denominator proves D(uv)=D(u)D(v), and conjugating an integral representative proves D(sigma u)=D(u). Also D(id)=1, so D(u^-1)=D(u)^-1.

For c=a/b in Q*, with a a nonzero integer and b a positive integer, use a denominator divisible by b and the multiplication-degree theorem to obtain

    D(cu)=c^4 D(u).

No degree is being assigned directly to a nonexistent algebraic morphism [1/b]. This formula uses the preceding definition on rational quasi-isogenies.

Set d_sigma=D(mu_sigma)^(1/4), choosing the positive real fourth root. These are positive real algebraic numbers. The discrepancy identity gives

    d_sigma d_tau = |c(sigma,tau)| d_sigma_tau.

Consequently its normalized scalar cocycle is

    epsilon(sigma,tau)
      = c(sigma,tau) d_sigma_tau / (d_sigma d_tau)
      = c(sigma,tau)/|c(sigma,tau)| in {+1,-1}.

Equivalently nu_sigma=d_sigma^-1 mu_sigma satisfies nu_sigma sigma(nu_tau)=epsilon(sigma,tau)nu_sigma_tau after extending the rational Hom spaces by real algebraic scalar coefficients, with trivial Galois action on this auxiliary coefficient field. The normalized nu_sigma are formal scalar-extended homomorphisms; the argument does not assert that they remain algebraic quasi-isogenies. One can avoid this notation entirely and use the displayed scalar cocycle formula. The cocycle identity follows by multiplying the original cocycle by the coboundary of d^-1. Positivity removes the fourth-root ambiguity.

sections.title: ## Conductor bridge, conditional on the actual representations

Fix a rational prime p and choose an auxiliary prime ell different from p. Suppose the actual geometric and modular two-dimensional ell-adic representations in one specified family are isomorphic as G_Q representations. Restriction gives an isomorphism on a decomposition group at p and on every inertia and ramification subgroup. The dimensions of inertia-invariants agree, as do all terms defining the Swan conductor. Therefore their Artin conductor exponents agree. This argument works separately for each constructed family; an isomorphism or endomorphism calculation for the b-family does not supply the beta-family premise.

An independent local compatibility/conductor theorem must identify the modular representation exponent with v_p(N_f), where N_f is the primitive newform's level. That theorem must cover p dividing N_f and the actual coefficient embedding. The Tate-module identification alone does not supply this assertion. A fixed auxiliary prime ell=3 cannot be used for this argument at p=3. sections.title: ## A056 normalization and guards
sections.claim_text: Work first in the generic coordinate ring y^2=x^3+Ax, and then specialize to the nonsingular fixed curve A=-d^2 over K0. Set psi_n=f_n for odd n and psi_n=2y f_n for even n. The initial values are f_0=0, f_1=f_2=1, f_3=3x^4+6Ax^2-A^2 and f_4=2(x^6+5Ax^4-5A^2x^2-A^3). The odd recurrence yields D0 L-R when m is even and L-D0 R when m is odd, where D0=(2y)^4=16(x^3+Ax)^2, L=f_{m+2}f_m^3, R=f_{m-1}f_{m+1}^3. The even recurrence cancels the even-index factors and gives f_{2m}=f_m(f_{m+2}f_{m-1}^2-f_{m-2}f_{m+1}^2) for m>=3; smaller indices are the bases. Every recursive index is smaller than the index being defined. The cancellations are polynomial identities before specialization, not division by an ordinate that might vanish.

sections.title: ## A056 exact scalar connection
sections.claim_text: The corrected omega_n=(psi_{n+2}psi_{n-1}^2-psi_{n-2}psi_{n+1}^2)/(4y) and the even recurrence give psi_{2n}=2psi_n omega_n; n=1,2 follow from the bases. Therefore 2y([n]P)psi_n(P)^4=psi_{2n}(P), while x([n]P)psi_n(P)^2=phi_n(P). For a nonidentity point P in the torsion-free carrier and n!=0, [n]P is not the identity, so psi_n(P)!=0 by the scalar-coordinate theorem and coprimality. With this guard, the two cleared equations uniquely recover both coordinates of [n]P. The inverse-norm guard is the separately supplied field encoding of nonzero elements of K0; it is not established by division polynomials. n=0 and identity P use their explicit identity branches. Negative n uses psi_{-n}=-psi_n and group negation, preserving the ordinate sign. This supplies current278–304 and its actual scalar-template use. The inaccessible Silverman errata are not a premise: closure-batch-010 supersedes the earlier A056 source-retrieval gap with the pinned Sutherland source. Existing finite scalar tests are supplementary checks, not the proof.

sections.title: ## A057 source and fixed-catalogue connection
sections.claim_text: Milne, Class Field Theory v4.03 (6August2020), ChapterV Theorem2.2, printed p.155: for every positive integer modulus m and every a coprime to m the rational primes congruent to a modulo m have Dirichlet density 1/phi(m), hence infinitely many. Exact PDF SHA256 50d79af78250a9f1117ad9d337e0b231704a533fc707966ed1bfa52e13d498f5; this is an author course note. In current306–308 set the fixed positive integer W=4 product_{p<=324}p. There are finitely many unit classes a modulo W. Each has infinitely many primes, and deleting the finite set <=324 leaves infinitely many. Ascending enumeration with finite trial primality tests and a congruence test therefore stops after finding22 in each class. The union is a fixed finite catalogue H_cat; its product with product_{p<=324}p defines N_s. This proves termination of this particular catalogue only, with no effective bound on its final prime and no claim about every later prime choice. The successful M0 index and its proof are separate.

sections.title: ## A058 class and unit sources
sections.claim_text: Milne, Algebraic Number Theory v3.08 (19July2020), Theorem4.3 printed p.70 and Theorem5.1 printed p.85: every ideal class has an integral representative with norm at most (n!/n^n)(4/pi)^r2 sqrt(|disc K|); the unit group of a number field is finitely generated with rank r1+r2-1 and torsion its roots of unity. Exact PDF SHA256 de2066ee7a319c0e6e521895a7e9e9567c2804bcafc0c8e67c417e508f2bc26b; these are author course notes. For K0=Q(s), s^2=2, its integral basis1,s gives discriminant8 and two real places. Minkowski bound is sqrt2<2, so the representative has norm1 and every ideal class is trivial. Roots of unity in a real field are +/-1, hence the units modulo squares have order4. The sign vectors of -1 and epsilon=1+s are independent, so this sign map on the four squareclasses is bijective and a totally positive unit is a square. This supplies current344–346. It does not claim epsilon is a chosen fundamental unit.

sections.title: ## A058 two-isogeny source
sections.claim_text: Silverman, Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, second edition2009, ChapterX Example4.8 printed p.336 and its connecting-homomorphism calculation continuing p.337 give the x-squareclass connecting map for a rational two-isogeny, with identity value1 and kernel-point value given by the linear coefficient. Exact PDF SHA256 72ee67bfa1e3fdf582ac7e4b032d7ca0b35a168ed6443ac39c121fbb788cab25. The displayed curve in Proposition4.9 p.337 misprints a^2-b for a^2-4b; we do not use that misprinted equation. The printed isogeny ordinate has the opposite sign from our convention, which leaves its image and kernel unchanged. The following explicit computation fixes the exact convention.

sections.title: ## A058 explicit kernel connection
sections.claim_text: For E_b:y^2=x^3+bx, b!=0 in characteristic0, set phi(x,y)=(x+b/x,y(1-b/x^2)) on nonzero x, and hatphi(X,Y)=((X-4b/X)/4,Y(1+4b/X^2)/8) on E_{-4b}. Substitution verifies the equations; the maps extend across their poles, send identity to identity, have kernels {O,(0,0)}, and hatphi phi=[2]. The last identity follows by the usual doubling formula, with x=(x^2-b)^2/(4x(x^2+b)) and ordinate sign fixed by the differential2. Define alpha_b(O)=1, alpha_b((0,0))=b, alpha_b(P)=x(P) modulo squares otherwise. The line-intersection equation gives product of three nonzero abscissas c^2, proving the homomorphism; tangents have repeated roots, a line through(0,0) gives x(P+(0,0))=b/x(P), and vertical pairs give a square. For Q=(X,Y), x(hatphi Q)=(Y/(2X))^2. Conversely if x(P)=u^2!=0, put v=y/u, X=2(x+v), Y=2uX. Since v^2=x^2+b and b!=0, X!=0; substitution gives Q on E_{-4b} and hatphi Q=P. If P=(0,0) and b is a square, Q=(2sqrt(b),0) is a lift; O lifts O. Thus ker(alpha_b)=hatphi(E_{-4b}(K)). Applying the same argument on the dual curve and scaling E_{16b} to E_b gives ker(alpha_{-4b})=phi(E_b(K)). These are the exact maps used in the local computation; no Selmer-group upper bound is silently identified with a rational-point image.

sections.title: ## A058 actual local descent
sections.claim_text: Set b=-d^2, d=75-53s with norm7. In the PID Z[s], (d) is a prime of norm7. For E the valuations of x away from(d) are even: if m=v(x) is odd, the unequal valuations3m and m of x^3 and -d^2x have an odd minimum, impossible for y^2. Consequently alpha(E) lies in the eight squareclasses generated by -1,epsilon,d. Rational two-torsion gives1,-1,d,-d. Since epsilon^4 d=delta=3-s, scaling (x,y) to(epsilon^4x,epsilon^6y) sends E to C:y^2=x^3-delta^2x. R=(epsilon,2s) lies on C by substitution and its squareclass is epsilon (the scale epsilon^4 is a square), so all eight classes occur. Independence follows from the d-valuation and the two independent unit signs.

sections.title: ## A058 dual and quotient
sections.claim_text: On E_{4d^2}, every nonzero x is positive at both real embeddings because y^2=x(x^2+4d^2). At primes other than(s),(d), the same odd-valuation argument applies. At(s), valuations of the two terms are3m and m+4; equality requires m=2, so odd m is impossible. At(d) they are3m and m+2; the only odd equality is m=1. Writing x=d u then gives y^2=d^3 u(u^2+4); an even valuation would require u^2=-4 modulo(d), impossible in F7 whose nonzero squares are1,2,4. Thus all valuations of x are even. The PID and total positivity make its squareclass trivial by the preceding unit result; the exceptional point(0,0) has class4d^2, also a square. Therefore alpha_{4d^2} is trivial, E_{4d^2}(K0)=phi E(K0), and ker(alpha_{-d^2})=hatphi phi E(K0)=2E(K0). Hence [E(K0):2E(K0)]=8. Equivalently the extra term in the two-isogeny quotient sequence vanishes: a nonkernel rational two-torsion point maps to the dual kernel. This supplies current348–362, not the independent full-torsion or height computation.

sections.title: ## A058 odd free index
sections.claim_text: Use the separately established rank1 and full rational two-torsion result for E, transported to C by the displayed isomorphism. Write the pulled-back R=mG+T with G a generator of the free quotient and T torsion. If m were even, the squareclass homomorphism would give alpha(R)=alpha(T), since alpha(2G)=1. But alpha(R)=epsilon has opposite real signs, whereas1,-1,d,-d have equal signs: d and its conjugate are positive since75>53sqrt2. Contradiction. Thus m is odd and nonzero. This proves the odd-index assertion at367–368 only; it does not show |m|=1. The separate height bound and finite enumeration still establish saturation.
